correctness.rationale: For 0<q<1, the facilitated Bernoulli resampling chain is reversible on its unique nonempty-vacancy component. Eliminating the filled-hub part of a hypothetical eigenvector for 0<λ<1−sqrt(1−q) produces the self-adjoint leaf-cube operator Bλ=H_leaf−μI+(μ−λ)P*, where μ=λ(1−λ)/(q−λ) satisfies 0<μ<1. Min–max bounds the second eigenvalue of Bλ below by 1−μ>0, while its constant Rayleigh quotient is strictly negative; consequently zero is not an eigenvalue. Leaf occupation contrasts provide explicit attaining eigenfunctions at λ*=1−sqrt(1−q). Pairing Bλ*g=0 with the first-level Walsh sum, nonzero at the all-filled leaf configuration, forces g to vanish at that configuration; the kernel then has exactly n−1 dimensions. For n=1 the three-state chain has eigenvalues 0,q,2−q. The standalone verifier replays 61,254 exact edge/eigenvector/reversibility comparisons and 21 numerical spectral-gap checks. Finite checks are not substituted for the all-size proof.

value.rationale: The FA-1f system is a canonical kinetically constrained stochastic spin model where vacancy facilitation creates relaxation bottlenecks. Determining the exact all-degree star spectral gap identifies a meaningful structural distinction: despite an increasing blocked-state population, the L² decay rate is degree-independent, while the slow eigenspace grows precisely with the n−1 independent leaf contrasts. The exceptional n=1 case makes the onset sharp. This is an exact infinite-family spectral property, not a single-instance eigenvalue, a routine substitution or a proxy for total-variation mixing.
